texts.preamble: Kr Puram Tr Ps vs Shankar Naika on 7 January, 2026 Kabc0D0223282017 In The Court Of Judicial Magistrate First Class Traffic Court-I At Mayohall, Bangalore. Present : Smt. Neelam Nitin Rao Judicial Magistrate First Class Traffic Court-I Bengaluru Dated 07th Day Of January 2026 C.C. No. 13438/2017
texts.facts: This case arises from the charge sheet filed by the PI of KR. Puram Traffic P. S. In Cr. No. 21/2017 against the accused for the alleged offence punishable under Section 279, 304(A) IPC. C.C. No. 13438/2017 2. On 01.07.2017 at 09.35 p.m., the accused was the driver of Lorry No. AP 27 TU 3949. He drove his Lorry on FCI Godown Road near Sudhir Way Bridge, from the old Madras Road towards FCI Godown, in a rash and negligent manner, to endanger human safety and dashed into a pedestrian, Sri Venkateshappa, who was crossing the Kr Puram Tr Ps vs Shankar Naika on 7 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15157879/ 1 road. When the pedestrian fell, the wheel of the lorry ran over the stomach of Venkateshappa. He sustained grievous blood injuries and succumbed to the occurrence. Thereby, the accused has committed an offence punishable under Section 279, 304(A) IPC. 3. After receipt of the complaint, the investigating officer visited the spot, conducted a mahazar in the presence of mahazar witnesses. Inquired and obtained statements of witnesses. After completion of the investigation filed charge sheet was filed against the accused for the offences p/u/s. 279, 304(A) IPC. 4. After filing the Charge Sheet, this court has verified all the prosecution records and considering that there are prima facie materials to proceed further against the accused, cognizance for the alleged offence p/u/s. 279, 304(A) IPC was taken, and a criminal case was registered against the accused in a register No. III, and a process was issued against the accused. 5. Pursuant to the summons, the accused appeared through his counsel and availed bail. Prosecution papers were supplied to the accused as contemplated under Section 207 of Cr.P.C. C.C. No. 13438/2017 6. Heard learned Sr APP and learned counsel for the accused, as there are no grounds to discharge the accused from the case, and there are materials to adjudicate the matter, hence, the substance of the accusation was framed. Read over and explained to the accused in the language best known to him. The accused pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried. Hence, the case was posted for prosecution evidence. Out of 13 witnesses, the prosecution has examined 6 witnesses as PW.1 to 6 and marked 12 documents as per Ex.P.1 to 12 and closed prosecution evidence. 7. After the conclusion of the prosecution evidence, the statement of the accused as required U/s. 313 Cr.P.C The accused denied all incriminating circumstances that appeared against him in the prosecution's evidence. Hence, the case was posted for arguments.
texts.arguments: 13. Learned Senior APP argued that the prosecution has proved its case against the accused beyond a reasonable doubt. The prosecution witnesses supported the case of prosecution. Hence, prayed for the conviction of the accused. 14. On the other hand, learned counsel for the accused argued that there is no corroboration available on record. Prosecution witnesses fully supported the case. Hence, prayed to acquit the accused. Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both. Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. 24.
